## Data assimilation and parameter recovery

Continuous data assimilation adds a feedback, or *nudging*, term to a model so
that it relaxes toward observations as they arrive. For a dissipative system

$$\frac{du}{dt} = G(u),$$

the assimilating system takes the form

$$\frac{d\tilde{u}}{dt} = G(\tilde{u}) - \mu I_h(\tilde{u} - u),$$

where $I_h$ projects onto the observed part of the state and $\mu$ sets the
relaxation rate. When enough length scales are observed and $\mu$ is chosen well,
$\tilde{u}$ converges to $u$ — including in the components never observed
directly.

The same feedback structure can be turned on the model's *parameters*, giving
algorithms that recover unknown coefficients on the fly, without ensembles or
repeated forward solves.
